mainTopic: Proving that a מסוכנת is not a טרפה and is permitted after שחיטה, and defining what counts as a מסוכנת
overview: The גמרא proves that a מסוכנת, an animal close to death, is not the same as a טרפה, so it is permitted once properly slaughtered. The first proof: if טרפה meant מסוכנת, the word נבלה in ויקרא 7:24 would be extra, since a קל וחומר could teach it. מר בר רב אשי suggests נבלה is needed for an animal killed instantly by being cut in half. The גמרא rejects this, because even that animal was מסוכנת for a moment. A second proof comes from the repeated word חלב, which hints at an animal whose fat is forbidden but whose meat is permitted: the מסוכנת. A third proof comes from יחזקאל, who boasted that he never ate 'כוס כוס' meat, an animal slaughtered in a rush before dying. That boast only makes sense if such meat is permitted. The גמרא then defines a מסוכנת as an animal that cannot stand even when helped up, even if it still eats wood chips or beams, and it gives the סורא and פומבדיתא versions of who said what. Finally, שמואל asks רב's students what רב said about a מסוכנת, and their answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If טרפה meant מסוכנת, the word נבלה would be extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא imagines that טרפה means מסוכנת. In that case the תורה would only need to attach the ban on eating the fat to טרפה, because a קל וחומר would already teach us the same for נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you think a טרפה is just a מסוכנת. Then the תורה should have written only: 'The fat of a נבלה may be used for any work, and the fat of a טרפה you shall not eat.' We would figure out the rest ourselves. If the איסור of טרפה can take effect on the איסור of חלב while the animal is still alive, then surely the איסור of נבלה, which comes after death, can take effect on it too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea that טרפה equals מסוכנת. It shows that this idea would make the word נבלה in the פסוק unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being מסוכנת already starts while the animal is alive. So if the איסור of טרפה (meaning מסוכנת) can sit on top of the איסור of חלב during life, it is a קל וחומר that נבלה can do so after death. If that were true, the תורה would not need to spell out נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect; forbidden to eat even after שחיטה
An animal in danger of dying soon, close to death
An animal that died without a proper שחיטה
Forbidden fat
It would enter your mind, meaning 'suppose you thought'
Is it even necessary to say? This signals a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: The imagined wording still mentions both נבלה and טרפה. The difference is where the ban on eating is placed. In the real פסוק, 'you shall not eat' covers both. In the גמרא's imagined version, נבלה is mentioned only for using the fat, and 'you shall not eat' is attached only to טרפה.

steps.raayaObject: That טרפה in the פסוק does not mean מסוכנת
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:24, together with a קל וחומר that would make נבלה unnecessary

steps.title: So טרפה is not the same as מסוכנת
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה did write נבלה, טרפה must mean something other than מסוכנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the תורה did write נבלה, we learn that טרפה is not the same as מסוכנת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion of the proof from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not waste words. Because נבלה was written even though a קל וחומר could have taught it, the starting idea must be wrong. So טרפה means an animal with a fatal defect, and a מסוכנת is a separate case that is permitted after שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, 'it follows that'
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: Rather, since the Merciful One wrote 'carcass,'
it follows that tereifa
is not the same as an animal in danger of dying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the extra word identified in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טרפה in the פסוק is not מסוכנת, so a מסוכנת is permitted after שחיטה.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: maybe נבלה is needed for an animal cut in half
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי suggests that טרפה could still mean מסוכנת. On this view, נבלה would be needed for a death that never passed through being מסוכנת, such as an animal cut in half.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי objected: Maybe, really, טרפה is the same as מסוכנת. As for your question, why the תורה needed to write נבלה: it is for a נבלה that does not come about through being מסוכנת. What case is that? Where someone cut the animal in half, like a broken pot.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי attacks the proof from steps 1 and 2. He finds a job for the word נבלה even if טרפה means מסוכנת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר only works for a נבלה that was first מסוכנת. If an animal is killed instantly, it skips that stage, so the קל וחומר doesn't cover it. That would explain why the תורה still had to write נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects, challenges strongly
But perhaps
A broken piece of pottery; here, an animal cut in half across its body
What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi objected to this:
But perhaps, really, I will tell you
a tereifa is the same as an animal in danger of dying,
and as for what you said:
'Why do I need the "carcass" that the Merciful One wrote?'
it is for that kind of carcass
that does not come about through being in danger of dying.
And what is the case?
Where he made it like a broken shard.
phrases.notes: He means the animal was cut in half across its body, so it died at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 2 by finding a separate use for the word נבלה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the word נבלה would be extra if טרפה meant מסוכנת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר doesn't cover a death that skips the מסוכנת stage, so נבלה is still needed for that case.

steps.title: Even an animal cut in half was מסוכנת for a moment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects מר בר רב אשי's case. Before the cut reached most of the body, the animal was already in danger of dying.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is impossible that the animal was not a little bit מסוכנת before he finished cutting through most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down מר בר רב אשי's objection, so the proof from steps 1 and 2 stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting an animal in half takes a moment. Partway through, before most of the body is cut, the animal is already close to death, which means it is מסוכנת. So every נבלה passes through being מסוכנת, and the קל וחומר would cover every case, making the word נבלה extra again.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible
A little, for a short time
The majority, most of it

phrases.english: There too, it is impossible
that it was not in danger of dying for a little bit
before he cut through the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case suggested in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: מר בר רב אשי's case of an animal cut in half (גיסטרא)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even that animal was מסוכנת for a moment, so it does not escape the קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: The first proof stands: טרפה is not מסוכנת, because otherwise the word נבלה in the פסוק would be extra.

steps.title: A second proof: why does the פסוק say חלב twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another proof. If מסוכנת were included in טרפה, the פסוק could have said 'the fat of נבלה and טרפה' once. Why repeat the word חלב?
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: If so, let the פסוק say 'the fat of a נבלה and טרפה.' Why do I need 'fat' and then 'fat' again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new, separate proof that a מסוכנת is permitted. It points to an extra word in the פסוק, and the next step will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real פסוק says 'חלב נבלה וחלב טרפה,' repeating the word חלב. A shorter wording, 'חלב נבלה וטרפה,' would have said the same thing. So the second חלב must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say; this introduces another answer or proof
Why do I need it? This points out an extra word

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
If so, let it say:
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if a מסוכנת really were counted as a טרפה.

phrases.english: 'The fat of a carcass and tereifa.'
Why do I need 'fat' and again 'fat'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a separate, second proof for the same conclusion as step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the repeated word חלב in the פסוק comes to teach

steps.title: The extra חלב hints at the מסוכנת, whose fat and meat differ
steps.stepSummary: The repeated חלב teaches that there are two kinds of animals. In a טרפה, fat and meat are both forbidden. In another kind, only the fat is forbidden and the meat is permitted, and that is the מסוכנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the טרפה) is the kind whose fat is not different from its meat. But you have another kind whose fat is different from its meat. Which one is that? The מסוכנת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the extra word חלב. It hints at the מסוכנת, whose fat is forbidden but whose meat is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a טרפה, the fat and the meat have the same status, since both are forbidden. The second חלב points to another animal where they have different statuses: the fat is forbidden as plain חלב, but the meat is permitted. That animal is the מסוכנת, so it is not a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Different, separate in status
Its meat
Another one

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs from the same פסוק show that a מסוכנת is not a טרפה. First, the word נבלה would otherwise be extra. Second, the repeated word חלב hints at an animal whose meat is permitted but whose fat is forbidden: the מסוכנת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halacha that an animal close to death may be eaten if it is slaughtered properly.

phrases.english: This is the one whose fat is not
different from its meat,
but you have another kind
whose fat is different from its meat,
and which one is that? An animal in danger of dying.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ הִיא שֶׁאֵין חֶלְבָּהּ חָלוּק מִבְּשָׂרָהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra חלב hints at the מסוכנת, whose fat is forbidden while its meat is permitted after שחיטה.

steps.title: Another proof from a פסוק in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another source on whether a מסוכנת is permitted: יחזקאל's statement that he never ate נבלה or טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like, learn it from here: 'Then I said: Ah, Lord God, my soul has not become impure, I have not eaten נבלה or טרפה from my youth until now, and no פיגול meat came into my mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a third source for the same point, after the two proofs from ויקרא 7:24 in steps 1–4 and 5–6. Here it only quotes the פסוק. The explanation and the proof come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken simply, the פסוק says יחזקאל avoided forbidden foods. The גמרא will read each phrase as describing extra piety beyond the strict law. That reading is what will show that a מסוכנת is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'rejected'. Normally a קרבן made unfit by wrong intentions. Here it will be read in a wider way.
'My soul has not become impure'

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is learned from here:
"Then I said: Ah, Lord God,
behold, my soul has not become impure;
and an unslaughtered carcass or a tereifa I have not eaten
from my youth until now,
and no piggul meat came into my mouth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, separate proof, this time from יחזקאל, for the idea already proven in steps 1–4 and 5–6: a slaughtered מסוכנת is permitted, so it is not a טרפה.
steps.raayaObject: That a מסוכנת is permitted when slaughtered, so it is not a טרפה

steps.title: Explaining each phrase of יחזקאל's statement
steps.stepSummary: Each phrase is read as extra piety. He avoided impure thoughts, meat slaughtered in a rush before death, meat permitted only by a חכם's ruling, and, according to רבי נתן, meat whose כהן gifts had not been separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My soul has not become impure' means he never had thoughts by day that would bring him to impurity at night. 'I have not eaten נבלה or טרפה' means he never ate meat of an animal slaughtered with a cry of 'slaughter it, slaughter it!' 'No פיגול meat' means he never ate from an animal that a חכם had to rule on. רבי נתן says it means he never ate from an animal whose gifts for the כהן had not been separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פסוק phrase by phrase. It shows that יחזקאל is describing things he avoided out of extra holiness, not just basic prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נבלה וטרפה' is read as 'כוס כוס' meat, meaning an animal so close to death that people rushed to slaughter it. That is exactly the מסוכנת. 'פיגול' is likewise read as meat that was technically permitted but somewhat doubtful.

keyTerms.meaning: I had thoughts (here, improper ones)
'Slaughter it, slaughter it!', meat from an animal slaughtered in a rush before it died
An animal that a חכם ruled on, because there was a question about it
Its gifts: the parts of an animal given to a כהן
Were separated

steps.confusionAlert: In this reading, 'נבלה וטרפה' does NOT mean a real נבלה or טרפה, since every Jew must avoid those. It means the מסוכנת, which is permitted but which יחזקאל avoided out of piety.

that I did not have improper thoughts during the day
that would bring me to impurity at night;
phrases.notes: He means impurity from a nighttime emission.

phrases.english: that I never ate meat of 'slaughter it, slaughter it';
phrases.notes: This is an animal so close to death that people shouted to slaughter it fast. That is the מסוכנת.

phrases.english: "And no piggul meat came into my mouth" means
that I never ate from an animal
about which a Sage had to issue a ruling.
phrases.notes: There was a question about it and a חכם ruled it permitted. He still stayed away.

phrases.english: In the name of רבי נתן they said:
that I never ate from an animal
whose gifts were not separated.
phrases.notes: These are the foreleg, jaw and maw, which go to the כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִנֵּה נַפְשִׁי לֹא מְטֻמָּאָה – שֶׁלֹּא הִרְהַרְתִּי בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 7, phrase by phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this פסוק, 'נבלה וטרפה' refers to 'כוס כוס' meat, the meat of a מסוכנת, which יחזקאל avoided out of extra piety.

steps.title: יחזקאל's boast proves a מסוכנת is permitted
steps.stepSummary: Avoiding a מסוכנת counts as greatness only if it is permitted. So a slaughtered מסוכנת must be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say it is permitted: then this is יחזקאל's greatness. But if you say it is forbidden, what is so great about יחזקאל avoiding it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now draws the proof from the reading in step 8. Praising someone for avoiding a forbidden food makes no sense, so the 'כוס כוס' meat must be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every Jew must avoid forbidden food, so avoiding it is no special praise. Since יחזקאל presents this as his piety, the מסוכנת must be kosher once slaughtered. This backs up the earlier conclusion that a מסוכנת is not a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works well if you say', which sets up a 'this works, that doesn't' proof
It is permitted
It is forbidden
His greatness

steps.whatToRemember: A מסוכנת, an animal near death, is kosher if properly slaughtered. Only very pious people avoid it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the proof that a מסוכנת is a separate category from טרפה. It sets up the practical question that comes next: how do we recognize a מסוכנת?

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is permitted,
that is the greatness of יחזקאל;
but if you say it is forbidden,
what is the greatness of יחזקאל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading from step 8 to prove that a מסוכנת is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל's statement, read as describing piety beyond the law

steps.title: What counts as a מסוכנת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to define an animal that is in danger of dying.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a מסוכנת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows a מסוכנת is permitted and asks how to identify one. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need a clear sign of when an animal is close enough to death to count as a מסוכנת. Its laws depend on recognizing it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is it like?', a request to define a case
An animal in danger of dying soon

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of an animal in danger of dying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving that a מסוכנת is permitted, the גמרא moves to defining it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The sign that identifies an animal as a מסוכנת

steps.title: רב: an animal that cannot stand even when helped up
steps.stepSummary: רב defines a מסוכנת as any animal that people try to stand up but that cannot stay standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: any animal that people stand up, and it does not stay standing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the sign of a מסוכנת: helped up, the animal still cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is the animal's ability to stand. Being unable to stay on its feet shows it is near death.

keyTerms.meaning: People stand it up
It does not stay standing

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said:
Any animal that people stand up on its feet
and it does not stay standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב כֹּל שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מסוכנת is an animal that cannot stand even when helped up.

steps.title: Even if it still eats wood or beams
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים add that an animal that cannot stand is a מסוכנת even if it still eats hard things like wood chips or even beams.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: even if it eats pieces of wood. רמי בר יחזקאל said: even if it eats beams.
steps.whatsHappening: These two statements widen רב's definition. Strong eating does not cancel the sign of not being able to stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A learner might think an animal with enough strength to chew wood is not near death. These אמוראים say the standing test decides anyway. רמי בר יחזקאל pushes it further: even chewing beams does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Pieces of split wood
Beams
Even

steps.whatToRemember: The sign of a מסוכנת is that it cannot stand when helped up. This holds even if it still eats strongly.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר:
phrases.english: רב חנינא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב:
Even if it eats pieces of wood.
רמי בר יחזקאל said:
Even if it eats beams.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ אוֹכֶלֶת בְּקָעִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רב's definition from step 11 to include an animal that still eats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that cannot stand is a מסוכנת even if it can still eat wood, or even beams.

steps.title: The פומבדיתא version opens with the same question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא labels the earlier version as the way it was taught in סורא. It then starts the פומבדיתא version, which opens with the same question: what is a מסוכנת?
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught it this way. In פומבדיתא they taught it this way: What is a מסוכנת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that the discussion we just learned is the סורא version. It is now setting up a second version, from פומבדיתא, which starts by asking the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question itself does not change. What changes in the פומבדיתא version is who said which part of the answer, as the next steps show. This is a real retelling by the גמרא, not a needless repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught, meaning this is how the lesson was passed down
סורא, the town of רב's yeshiva
פומבדיתא, the town of the other great Babylonian yeshiva
An animal in danger of dying soon

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the same question as Step 10, now told the way פומבדיתא remembered it.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught it this way.
phrases.notes: "This way" means the version we just learned in Steps 10–12.

phrases.english: In Pumbedita they taught it this way:
What is considered an animal in danger of dying?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנֵי הָכִי. בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Labels Steps 10–12 as the סורא version and begins the פומבדיתא version of the same exchange.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to define a מסוכנת, according to the פומבדיתא tradition.

steps.title: רב's definition, including the wood chips
steps.stepSummary: In the פומבדיתא version, רב יהודה quotes רב: a מסוכנת is any animal that people try to stand up but cannot stay standing, even if it still eats wood chips.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is any animal that people stand up and it does not stay standing, even if it eats pieces of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by quoting רב. In this version, רב himself adds that eating wood chips does not help the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is the same as in Step 11: if it cannot stand, it is a מסוכנת. The difference is that the wood-chips line is now part of רב's own words. Even a strong jaw does not cancel the sign of weak legs.

keyTerms.meaning: They stand it up, meaning people try to get the animal on its feet
It does not stay standing
Pieces or chips of wood, which are hard to chew

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Any animal that people stand up on its feet
but it does not stay standing,
even if it eats pieces of wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ וְאֵינָהּ עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 within the פומבדיתא version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מסוכנת is an animal that cannot stay standing when stood up, even if it eats wood chips.

steps.title: Even eating beams does not help
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל goes further: even if the animal eats whole beams, it is still a מסוכנת if it cannot stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל said: Even if it eats beams.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר יחזקאל adds a stronger example to רב's rule. Even an animal strong enough to chew beams counts as a מסוכנת if it cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beams are much bigger and harder than wood chips. So רמי בר יחזקאל is saying that not standing is the deciding sign, no matter how strong the animal's eating looks.

keyTerms.meaning: Beams, large pieces of wood

steps.whatToRemember: In the פומבדיתא version, רב's own words include the wood chips, and רמי בר יחזקאל adds beams. Either way, if the animal cannot stand, it is a מסוכנת, however well it eats.

phrases.english: Rami bar Yeḥezkel said:
Even if it eats beams.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ אוֹכֶלֶת קוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רב's definition from Step 14 with a stronger example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that cannot stand is a מסוכנת even if it eats beams.

steps.title: שמואל asks רב's students what רב said
steps.stepSummary: שמואל meets רב's students and asks them what רב said about a מסוכנת. They begin to answer: 'This is what רב said.'
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל found students of רב. He said to them: What did רב say about a מסוכנת? They said to him: This is what רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: A short story begins in which שמואל asks רב's students for רב's teaching on a מסוכנת. This step sets up their answer, which comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל wants to hear רב's view straight from the students who learned from him. The step ends right as they start quoting רב, so the actual content is still to come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both versions of רב's definition, a story begins in which שמואל asks for רב's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רב taught about how to define a מסוכנת, as his students heard it.
